title: Average Nurse Salary Australia: Award Rates, Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top
description: Find the average nurse salary Australia using Fair Work award rates. Learn how to convert hourly to annual pay, including casual loading and super paid on top.
salarySummary: Under the Nurses Award 2020, a full-time Registered Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 earns $32.09 per hour, or $63,416 per year based on 38 hours per week for 52 weeks.

faqs.q: What is the average nurse salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The average nurse salary in Australia varies by role and experience. Under the Nurses Award 2020, minimum hourly rates range from $27.65 for a 1st-year nursing assistant to $52.50 for a Level 4 Grade 2 registered nurse. Many nurses earn above these award minimums, with the Australian Bureau of Statistics reporting full-time adult average weekly earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026), which equates to about $108,352 per year. However, actual pay depends on classification, shift penalties, and enterprise agreements.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to nurse pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Nurses Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate for their classification. For example, a Registered Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 has a base rate of $32.09 per hour; with casual loading the rate becomes $40.11 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. The loading is applied before any penalty rates or overtime.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the hourly rate. Under the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must contribute 12% of ordinary earnings (as of 2026–27) to a super fund. This is in addition to the base salary. For a nurse earning $32.09 per hour, the super contribution is about $3.85 per hour, making the total cost to the employer $35.94 per hour. The maximum contribution base is capped at $270,830 per quarter.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the average nurse salary Australia

When you search for the **average nurse salary Australia, it’s important to distinguish between award minimum rates and actual average earnings. The and the provide the official minimum rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The gives the full pay guide for the Nurses Award 2020. These sources are more reliable than recruiter surveys.

### How to convert hourly to annual pay

The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time nurses, the award states ordinary hours of 38 per week (see ). So a Registered Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 at $32.09 per hour earns:

- **Weekly**: $32.09 × 38 = $1,219.42
- **Fortnightly**: $1,219.42 × 2 = $2,438.84
- **Annual**: $1,219.42 × 52 = $63,409.84

This is the minimum annual salary for that classification. Many nurses earn more through higher pay points, allowances, or enterprise agreements.

### Award rates for nurses under the Nurses Award 2020

The Nurses Award 2020 (MA000034) covers most nurses and assistants. The summary shows a wide range:

| Classification | Hourly rate | Annual (38h/wk) |
|----------------|-------------|----------------|
| Nursing assistant 1st year | $27.65 | $54,636 |
| Enrolled nurse pay point 1 | $30.00 | $59,280 |
| Registered nurse level 1 pay point 1 | $32.09 | $63,410 |
| Registered nurse level 1 pay point 8 | $38.57 | $76,239 |
| Registered nurse level 2 pay point 4 | $41.59 | $82,194 |
| Registered nurse level 4 grade 2 | $52.50 | $103,740 |

These are minimum rates. The **average nurse salary Australia** is likely higher, especially for experienced nurses in higher classifications. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports full-time adult average weekly earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026), which is about $108,352 per year – a useful benchmark.

### Casual loading for nurses

Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, a casual Registered Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1:

- Base rate: $32.09
- Casual loading (25%): $8.02
- Casual hourly rate: $40.11

This loading is paid instead of sick leave, annual leave, and public holiday pay. The page explains that casual loading is added after any shift loadings. When using the [timesheet calculator, you can check the “casual loading option to see the effect.

### Superannuation is paid on top

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings (2026–27), paid by the employer **on top** of the salary. It is not deducted from the hourly rate. For a nurse earning $32.09 per hour, the super contribution is $3.85 per hour, making the total cost $35.94 per hour. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. This is important when comparing salary packages.

### Tax considerations

Tax is calculated on the annual gross salary. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (single threshold $24,276 for 2025–26). For a nurse earning $63,410, the tax would be approximately $9,567 plus Medicare $1,268, leaving about $52,575 after tax. This is an estimate.

### Using the timesheet calculator

You can use the [timesheet](/) to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. The calculator also shows the effect of casual loading and super. For more details on award rates, see the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).

### Summary

The average nurse salary Australia depends on classification, experience, and whether you are permanent or casual. The Nurses Award 2020 sets minimums, but many nurses earn above these. Always check your award or enterprise agreement. Remember that super is paid on top, and casual loading adds 25% to the base rate. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see your own figures.
